message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We show that for all functions
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(t(n) \ge n\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , every multitape Turing machine running in time
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">t</jats:italic>
                    can be simulated in space only
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(O(\sqrt {t \log t})\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . This is a substantial improvement over Hopcroft, Paul, and Valiant’s simulation of time
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">t</jats:italic>
                    in
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(O(t/\log t)\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    space from 50 years ago [FOCS 1975, JACM 1977]. Among other results, our simulation implies that bounded fan-in circuits of size
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">s</jats:italic>
                    can be evaluated on any input in only
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\sqrt {s} \cdot \text{poly}(\log s)\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    space, and that there are explicit problems solvable in
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(O(n)\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    space which require
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(n^{2-\varepsilon }\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    time on a multitape Turing machine for all
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\varepsilon \gt 0\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , thereby making a little progress on the
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\({\sf P}\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    versus
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\({\sf PSPACE}\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    problem.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Our simulation reduces the problem of simulating time-bounded multitape Turing machines to a series of implicitly-defined Tree Evaluation instances with nice parameters, leveraging the remarkable space-efficient algorithm for Tree Evaluation recently found by Cook and Mertz [STOC 2024].</jats:p>
title: Simulating Time with Square-Root Space
